techniques.title: Shell metacharacter injection through MCP tool parameters
techniques.mechanism: Unsanitized MCP tool input reaches execSync/exec, yielding RCE on the server host.

techniques.title: curl-fallback command injection in an MCP server
techniques.mechanism: A failed fetch falls back to exec'ing curl with an unsanitized URL, enabling RCE.

techniques.title: Command injection in a scaffolded MCP stdio server
techniques.mechanism: Generated server concatenates tool input into exec(), giving RCE to anything built from it.

techniques.title: Line-jumping — tool-description injection at listing time
techniques.mechanism: Hidden instructions in a tool description enter the model context at tools/list, before any call.

techniques.title: Rug pull — silent mutation of an approved tool
techniques.mechanism: A server approved once later changes a tool's definition with no integrity re-check.

techniques.title: Missing-auth MCP proxy command execution
techniques.mechanism: No auth between client and MCP proxy lets any local/web-driven request spawn MCP processes.

techniques.title: RCE from a malicious upstream MCP server
techniques.mechanism: A client is RCE'd via a crafted authorization_endpoint URL in an untrusted server's response.

techniques.title: DNS-rebinding to a localhost MCP server
techniques.mechanism: A malicious page rebinds DNS to reach an unauthenticated localhost MCP server cross-origin.

techniques.title: Session ID / auth token placed in a URL query string
techniques.mechanism: A credential in the query string leaks via server logs, proxies, CDNs, history, and Referer.

techniques.title: Serialized-object smuggling through an LLM response field
techniques.mechanism: Injected output carries a serialization marker; deserialization rehydrates it as trusted and exfiltrates secrets.

techniques.title: Persistent memory / context-store poisoning
techniques.mechanism: Attacker-controlled content is written into data the agent later reads back as trusted context.

techniques.title: Indirect prompt injection via tool / API response
techniques.mechanism: Malicious text in returned tool data overrides the agent's plan and redirects its actions.

techniques.title: System-prompt / guardrail extraction to plan evasion
techniques.mechanism: Crafted queries coerce the agent to reveal its hidden system prompt, exposing control logic.

evidence.label: MITRE ATLAS — Extract LLM System Prompt

techniques.title: Confused-deputy token passthrough in an MCP server
techniques.mechanism: A server forwards a held token to a downstream API without audience validation, escalating privilege.

techniques.title: Agent reads .env / secret files without consent
techniques.mechanism: An agent tool reads credential files (.env, credentials, .npmrc) outside any user-approved scope.

techniques.title: Hallucinated-dependency squatting (slopsquatting)
techniques.mechanism: The model recommends a fabricated package name an attacker pre-registers, pulling code into the agent env.

techniques.title: Path-traversal blacklist bypass via non-canonical paths
techniques.mechanism: Exact-string path checks are bypassed with ../, /./, redundant slashes to reach sensitive files.

techniques.title: MCP filesystem sandbox escape via symlink following
techniques.mechanism: A symlink inside an allowed directory resolves to an out-of-scope path, granting system file access.

techniques.title: Prompt-injection-to-RCE via an agent's file-write capability
techniques.mechanism: Injected instructions drive the agent to write a startup/config file that yields persistent code execution.

techniques.title: Agent Card poisoning to capture A2A task routing
techniques.mechanism: A rogue A2A agent advertises an instruction-laden Agent Card so the orchestrator routes tasks to it.

techniques.title: Cross-agent injection propagation (cascading compromise)
techniques.mechanism: One compromised agent emits content that injects the next downstream agent, cascading through the swarm.

techniques.title: Trace tampering / non-tamper-evident agent audit logs
techniques.mechanism: An agent logs reasoning but not the actual tool call, or logs are mutable — defeating after-the-fact audit.

evidence.label: EU AI Act Art.12 logging / observability gap

techniques.title: Adversarial transaction steering of a purchasing agent
techniques.mechanism: Injected content in a listing/page steers an autonomous-commerce agent to overpay or leak payment authority.

techniques.title: Payment-mandate forgery in an agent-to-agent handshake
techniques.mechanism: A rogue agent spoofs delegated payment authority or mandate scope in an agentic-commerce exchange.
